key_insight: The paper reframes on-policy distillation as an RL problem and proposes Least-Square Policy Distillation (LSPD) to improve sample efficiency, exploration, and policy diversity for LLM reasoning.
engineering_relevance: For computational systems that train reasoning models, LSPD offers a more rollout-efficient distillation pipeline that can reuse prior trajectories while maintaining strong performance.
method: Connect OPD’s reverse-KL objective to KL-regularized policy optimization.
Introduce optimistic exploration plus off-policy data reuse in a least-squares distillation framework.
Provide theory linking LSPD to optimistic value-based learning with \tilde{\mathcal O}(\log K) regret in the idealized online setting.
evidence_signal: Across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks and diverse teacher-student setups, LSPD improves Avg@16 by +1.59 points on average and its off-policy variant matches vanilla OPD using only the first 25% of rollout batches.
watch_item: The strongest guarantees are for an idealized formulation, so practical gains may depend on stable exploration, trajectory reuse quality, and careful implementation of off-policy training.
paper_title: An RL View of OPD: Least Square Policy Distillation for Sample-Efficient LLM Reasoning
